<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead" summary="Move app behind /app with sidebar shell">
Restructure /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/cleaner_crm: move the authenticated app behind an /app scope with a drawer+sidebar app layout, exactly following the reference implementation in /Users/johndavenport/Documents/github/get_ai_traffic (READ these first: lib/get_ai_traffic_web/router.ex lines 140-230 for the /app scope shape, and lib/get_ai_traffic_web/components/layouts.ex for the drawer+sidebar Layouts.app).

MCP note: on "No session_id available" add session_id "b82dc084-1093-4624-b490-31c68a31a4a8"; if MCP hangs >2 min, message me and keep coding. Do NOT touch the running UAT deploy or dev _build; do not run `kamal` or deploy scripts.

ROUTE MAPPING (old → new). Everything authenticated moves under /app:
- /field, /field/jobs/:id → /app/field, /app/field/jobs/:id (cleaner side is app chrome too)
- /users/settings[/confirm-email/:token] → /app/users/settings[...]
- /accounts* (index/new/:id/edit/picker/manage/members/invitations) → /app/accounts*
- /integrations → /app/integrations
- /clients*, /properties* → /app/clients*, /app/properties*
- /schedule* (board/plans/jobs/cleaners/time-off) → /app/schedule*
- /audit → /app/audit; /quotes* (incl rate-card) → /app/quotes*; /quality* → /app/quality*; /timesheets (+ GET /timesheets/export controller route) → /app/timesheets*; /invoices* → /app/invoices*; /reminders (office log) → /app/reminders; /reviews (office inbox ReviewLive.Index) → /app/reviews; /settings/booking → /app/settings/booking
STAYS OUTSIDE /app (public/token/webhook/auth plumbing): /, /book*, /portal*, /portal/access/:token, /reviews/:token (public review page — nice: no more collision with the office inbox), /pay/:token, /reminders/confirm/:token + /reminders/reschedule/:token, /webhooks/*, /users/log-in, /users/log-in/:token, /users/register, /users/log-out, POST /users/update-password, /integrations/oauth/:provider + callback (external redirect URIs — MUST stay put), invitations accept token route.

ROUTER SHAPE (mirror get_ai_traffic): one `scope "/app"` with pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user] containing three live_sessions: (1) :require_authenticated_user — users/settings, accounts* (the onboarding landing; NO RequireAccount here or account creation becomes unreachable), integrations; (2) :require_account — field routes ({UserAuth, :require_authenticated} + {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default}); (3) :require_office_role — all office routes (UserAuth + RequireAccount + RequireOfficeRole, as today). Keep the existing hooks/modules; only paths move. RequireOfficeRole's redirect target becomes /app/field; RequireAccount's stays /app/accounts/new (adjust path).

LAYOUT: rewrite the :app variant of CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts.app as the get_ai_traffic drawer+sidebar (drawer lg:drawer-open, header with mobile hamburger + account-name breadcrumb linking to /app/accounts/picker + our EXISTING theme_toggle — keep ours, not theirs; sidebar: brand at top linking "/", role-aware menu — office role: Schedule, Clients, Quotes, Invoices, Timesheets, Quality, Reviews, Reminders, Audit, then a divider, Field view; everyone: My Day (cleaners' label for /app/field); divider then Settings group: Rate card, Booking policy, Accounts, Integrations, User settings (office-only items only for office roles); sidebar footer: user email + Log out via method=delete). Keep the :public and :portal variants exactly as they are today (top-bar style). Keep nav_role/signed_in_home helpers working; signed_in_home targets become /app/schedule, /app/field, /app/accounts/new. Landing page home.html.heex "Go to app"/links update accordingly.

SWEEP (~144 files reference old paths): update every ~p sigil, push_navigate/redirect target, and test/spex assertion across lib/ and test/ (unit tests, LiveView tests, ALL spex under test/spex/, Wallaby journeys under test/journeys/, layouts tests). Careful non-mechanical cases: ~p"/reviews/#{token}" (public, unchanged) vs ~p"/reviews" (office → /app/reviews); ~p"/reminders/confirm..." (unchanged) vs ~p"/reminders" (office); /users/settings → /app/users/settings but /users/log-in|register|log-out unchanged; /integrations → /app/integrations but /integrations/oauth/* unchanged; /settings/booking → /app/settings/booking. Also UserAuth's signed-in redirect path(s) if hardcoded, invitation acceptance redirects, notifier emails that link to app pages, and docs/qa scripts are OUT of scope (skip .code_my_spec/).

VERIFY (the bar): MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors clean; FULL PORT=4002 MIX_ENV=test mix test green (266+, Wallaby included — kill port 4002 first: lsof -ti :4002 | xargs kill -9); FULL PORT=4002 mix spex green (143); mix format. Add/keep a layouts test asserting the sidebar renders office links for owners and not for cleaners.

Final response: route-map summary, layout notes, test counts, files-changed count, "NEEDS RELEASE REBUILD". Under 200 words.
</teammate-message>

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- stripe:explain-error: Explain Stripe error codes and provide solutions with code examples
- stripe:test-cards: Display Stripe test card numbers for various testing scenarios
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- stripe:connect-recommend: This skill should be used when the user asks about Stripe Connect configuration, charge patterns, dashboard access, or how to get started with Connect, is building a marketplace, platform, multi-vendor store, gig platform, or subscription platform, needs to pay out sellers, vendors, or providers, mentions split payments, revenue sharing, multi-party payments, or similar payment distribution concepts, provides a company URL or business description for a recommendation, builds SaaS that routes money between parties (e.g. POS, booking, invoicing — not operational SaaS without payment routing), asks about onboarding or KYC for merchants/sellers/vendors, mentions connected account dashboard or responsibility configurations, or asks about payment flows, white-label payments, or embedded payments.
- stripe:stripe-best-practices: Guides Stripe integration decisions — API selection (Checkout Sessions vs PaymentIntents), Connect platform setup (Accounts v2, controller properties), billing/subscriptions, Treasury financial accounts, integration surfaces (Checkout, Payment Element), migrating from deprecated Stripe APIs, and security best practices (API key management, restricted keys, webhooks, OAuth). Use when building, modifying, or reviewing any Stripe integration — including accepting payments, building marketplaces, integrating Stripe, processing payments, setting up subscriptions, creating connected accounts, or implementing secure key handling.
- stripe:stripe-directory: Use when the user wants to find businesses, software, service providers, or partners for a specific industry, workflow, pain point, capability, or job to be done. Also use when the agent needs to programmatically purchase or consume a service. Use Stripe Directory to build a short relevant shortlist, even if the user does not mention Stripe Directory explicitly.
- stripe:stripe-projects: Use when the user wants to provision infrastructure or third-party services using Stripe Projects. Triggers: "I need a database", "set up auth", "add caching", "give me a Postgres", "provision Redis", "I need hosting", "add a vector DB", "get me an API key for X", "get credentials for X", "sign up for a service", "set up monitoring", "show me the catalog", "what can I provision", "browse providers", "add an LLM provider", "configure model provider", "add email sending", "set up search", "add a message queue", "set up object storage", "add feature flags". Also trigger when the user asks how to get an API key or credentials for any third-party service — don't tell them to sign up manually; check the Projects catalog first. Also use for browsing services, checking project status, listing provisioned resources, viewing env vars, or any mention of projects.dev or adding/provisioning/connecting a cloud service.
- stripe:upgrade-stripe: Guide for upgrading Stripe API versions and SDKs
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	defmodule GetAiTrafficWeb.Router do
2	  use GetAiTrafficWeb, :router
3	
4	  import GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth
5	
6	  pipeline :browser do
7	    plug :accepts, ["html"]
8	    plug :fetch_session
9	    plug :fetch_live_flash
10	    plug :put_root_layout, html: {GetAiTrafficWeb.Layouts, :root}
11	    plug :protect_from_forgery
12	    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
13	    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
14	  end
15	
16	  pipeline :api do
17	    plug :accepts, ["json"]
18	  end
19	
20	  pipeline :mcp_protected do
21	    plug :accepts, ["json", "sse"]
22	    plug GetAiTrafficWeb.Plugs.RequireOauthToken
23	  end
24	
25	  # OAuth 2.1 authorization server (backs the MCP auth). See the anubis-mcp ADR.
26	  # Browser consent flow (session + CSRF).
27	  scope "/oauth", GetAiTrafficWeb do
28	    pipe_through :browser
29	
30	    get "/authorize", OAuthController, :authorize
31	    post "/authorize", OAuthController, :create
32	    delete "/authorize", OAuthController, :delete
33	  end
34	
35	  # OAuth token + dynamic client registration (no CSRF).
36	  scope "/oauth", GetAiTrafficWeb do
37	    pipe_through :api
38	
39	    post "/token", OAuthController, :token
40	    post "/revoke", OAuthController, :revoke
41	    post "/register", OAuthController, :register
42	  end
43	
44	  # MCP clients fall back to POST /register when they can't read AS metadata.
45	  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
46	    pipe_through :api
47	
48	    post "/register", OAuthController, :register
49	  end
50	
51	  # OAuth discovery (RFC 8414 / 9728) — what the MCP client probes first.
52	  scope "/.well-known", GetAiTrafficWeb do
53	    pipe_through :api
54	
55	    get "/oauth-protected-resource", OAuthController, :protected_resource_metadata
56	    get "/oauth-protected-resource/*path", OAuthController, :protected_resource_metadata
57	    get "/oauth-authorization-server", OAuthController, :authorization_server_metadata
58	    get "/oauth-authorization-server/*path", OAuthController, :authorization_server_metadata
59	  end
60	
61	  # MCP server (Anubis StreamableHTTP transport) — the account-scoped surface the
62	  # outer agent drives. See the anubis-mcp ADR.
63	  scope "/" do
64	    pipe_through :mcp_protected
65	
66	    forward "/mcp/cms", Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug,
67	      server: GetAiTraffic.McpServers.CmsServer
68	
69	    forward "/mcp", Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug,
70	      server: GetAiTraffic.McpServers.WorkflowServer
71	  end
72	
73	  # Content sync endpoint — the CodeMySpec publishing flow POSTs the content
74	  # corpus here. Authenticated by a deployment key (Bearer DEPLOY_KEY), not OAuth.
75	  scope "/api/content", GetAiTrafficWeb do
76	    pipe_through :api
77	
78	    post "/sync", ContentSyncController, :sync
79	  end
80	
81	  # Registered-users endpoint — the CodeMySpec dashboard GETs this to list the
82	  # app's users. Authenticated by the same deployment key (Bearer DEPLOY_KEY).
83	  scope "/api/cms", GetAiTrafficWeb do
84	    pipe_through :api
85	
86	    get "/users", CmsUsersController, :index
87	  end
88	
89	  # Stripe webhook (story 757) — no CSRF/auth; authenticated by HMAC signature
90	  # against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET inside the controller.
91	  scope "/webhooks", GetAiTrafficWeb do
92	    pipe_through :api
93	
94	    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :handle
95	  end
96	
97	  # Lightweight liveness probe for Docker/Caddy health checks — no pipeline
98	  # (no session, CSRF, or DB), just a 200.
99	  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
100	    get "/health", PageController, :health
101	  end
102	
103	  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
104	    pipe_through :browser
105	
106	    # Content index pages
107	    get "/blog", ContentController, :blog_index
108	    get "/documentation", ContentController, :documentation_index
109	    get "/pages", ContentController, :pages_index
110	
111	    # Content show pages
112	    get "/blog/:slug", ContentController, :blog
113	    get "/documentation/:slug", ContentController, :documentation
114	    get "/pages/:slug", ContentController, :page
115	
116	    get "/pricing", PageController, :pricing
117	    get "/", PageController, :home
118	  end
119	
120	  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
121	  # scope "/api", GetAiTrafficWeb do
122	  #   pipe_through :api
123	  # end
124	
125	  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
126	  if Application.compile_env(:get_ai_traffic, :dev_routes) do
127	    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
128	    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
129	    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
130	    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
131	    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
132	    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router
133

defmodule GetAiTrafficWeb.Router do
  use GetAiTrafficWeb, :router

  import GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {GetAiTrafficWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  pipeline :mcp_protected do
    plug :accepts, ["json", "sse"]
    plug GetAiTrafficWeb.Plugs.RequireOauthToken
  end

  # OAuth 2.1 authorization server (backs the MCP auth). See the anubis-mcp ADR.
  # Browser consent flow (session + CSRF).
  scope "/oauth", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/authorize", OAuthController, :authorize
    post "/authorize", OAuthController, :create
    delete "/authorize", OAuthController, :delete
  end

  # OAuth token + dynamic client registration (no CSRF).
  scope "/oauth", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :api

    post "/token", OAuthController, :token
    post "/revoke", OAuthController, :revoke
    post "/register", OAuthController, :register
  end

  # MCP clients fall back to POST /register when they can't read AS metadata.
  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :api

    post "/register", OAuthController, :register
  end

  # OAuth discovery (RFC 8414 / 9728) — what the MCP client probes first.
  scope "/.well-known", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :api

    get "/oauth-protected-resource", OAuthController, :protected_resource_metadata
    get "/oauth-protected-resource/*path", OAuthController, :protected_resource_metadata
    get "/oauth-authorization-server", OAuthController, :authorization_server_metadata
    get "/oauth-authorization-server/*path", OAuthController, :authorization_server_metadata
  end

  # MCP server (Anubis StreamableHTTP transport) — the account-scoped surface the
  # outer agent drives. See the anubis-mcp ADR.
  scope "/" do
    pipe_through :mcp_protected

    forward "/mcp/cms", Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug,
      server: GetAiTraffic.McpServers.CmsServer

    forward "/mcp", Anubis.Server.Transport.StreamableHTTP.Plug,
      server: GetAiTraffic.McpServers.WorkflowServer
  end

  # Content sync endpoint — the CodeMySpec publishing flow POSTs the content
  # corpus here. Authenticated by a deployment key (Bearer DEPLOY_KEY), not OAuth.
  scope "/api/content", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :api

    post "/sync", ContentSyncController, :sync
  end

  # Registered-users endpoint — the CodeMySpec dashboard GETs this to list the
  # app's users. Authenticated by the same deployment key (Bearer DEPLOY_KEY).
  scope "/api/cms", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :api

    get "/users", CmsUsersController, :index
  end

  # Stripe webhook (story 757) — no CSRF/auth; authenticated by HMAC signature
  # against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET inside the controller.
  scope "/webhooks", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :api

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :handle
  end

  # Lightweight liveness probe for Docker/Caddy health checks — no pipeline
  # (no session, CSRF, or DB), just a 200.
  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    get "/health", PageController, :health
  end

  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    # Content index pages
    get "/blog", ContentController, :blog_index
    get "/documentation", ContentController, :documentation_index
    get "/pages", ContentController, :pages_index

    # Content show pages
    get "/blog/:slug", ContentController, :blog
    get "/documentation/:slug", ContentController, :documentation
    get "/pages/:slug", ContentController, :page

    get "/pricing", PageController, :pricing
    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", GetAiTrafficWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:get_ai_traffic, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: GetAiTrafficWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authenticated app surface

  # Every LiveView under /app/* is the "app" chrome (sidebar shell via
  # Layouts.app). The /app prefix is the source of truth that distinguishes the
  # app layout from the public content layout (`/`, `/blog`, ...).
  scope "/app", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    # Authenticated, no account required. /app (Overview) is the onboarding
    # landing — it forces account creation inline when the user has none, and
    # account management lives here so users can always reach the picker.
    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/", AppLive.Overview, :index

      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/billing", BillingLive.Index, :index

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show
    end

    # Account-scoped product surface — gated on account membership so users
    # without an account are bounced to /app to create one first.
    live_session :require_active_account,
      on_mount: [
        {GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth, :require_account_membership}
      ] do
      live "/sites", SiteLive.Index, :index
      live "/sites/new", SiteLive.Index, :new
      live "/sites/:id/edit", SiteLive.Index, :edit
      live "/sites/:id/connect", SiteLive.Connection, :show
      live "/sites/:id", SiteLive.Show, :show

      live "/audits/:id", ActionItemLive.Index, :index
      live "/audits/:audit_id/agent", AgentRunLive.Show, :show
      live "/audits/:audit_id/fixes", AuditFixesLive.Show, :show
      live "/audits/:audit_id/proposals", ContentProposalLive.Index, :index
      live "/audits/:audit_id/items/:id", ActionItemLive.Show, :show
    end

    live_session :require_admin,
      on_mount: [
        {GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth, :require_admin}
      ] do
      live "/admin/topics", Admin.TopicLive.Index, :index
      live "/admin/topics/new", Admin.TopicLive.Index, :new
      live "/admin/topics/gaps", Admin.TopicLive.Index, :gaps
    end
  end

  # Authenticated routes that must stay at the root path (not under /app):
  # the OAuth connect/callback URLs are registered with external providers
  # (Google/GitHub redirect URIs), and the password-update form posts here.
  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password

    scope "/integrations/oauth" do
      get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
      get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
    end
  end

  scope "/", GetAiTrafficWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{GetAiTrafficWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new

      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    post "/users/register-login", UserSessionController, :register_login
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index
    end

    # Field surfaces need an active account: every scoped query guards
    # on `active_account_id`, so a freshly-registered user with no
    # company is funneled to /accounts/new instead of crashing.
    live_session :require_account,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default}
      ] do
      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above. RequireAccount runs
    # first so an account-less user goes to company creation, not into
    # RequireOfficeRole's /field redirect (which would also crash).
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/rate-card", QuoteLive.RateCard, :edit
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index

      live "/settings/booking", SettingsLive.BookingPolicy, :edit
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout —
  # while the owner's review inbox is office-only, gated the same way
  # as the other office surfaces above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :reviews_office,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index
    end
  end

  # Portal (client magic-link) — no user auth. `/portal/access/:token`
  # exchanges a mailed/booking-issued token for a portal session
  # (plain `:browser`, like the reminder confirm/reschedule links
  # above, so `fetch_session`/`fetch_current_scope_for_user` still
  # run); every other portal route sits behind
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s own session check instead.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    get "/portal/access/:token", PortalController, :access

    live_session :portal,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
      live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      live "/portal/visits/:id", PortalLive.Visit, :show
      live "/portal/invoices", PortalLive.Invoices, :index
    end
  end

  # Public booking funnel (stories 848/849) — no user auth, plain
  # `:browser` (like the reminder/reviews/portal public routes above)
  # so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout. Both routes
  # share one view module, `BookingLive.Quote` — see its moduledoc for
  # why `BookingLive.Accept` isn't routed on its own.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :public_booking,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/book", BookingLive.Quote, :new
      live "/book/accept/:token", BookingLive.Quote, :accept
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts do @moduledoc """ This module holds layouts and related functionality used by your application. """ use CleanerCrmWeb, :html alias CleanerCrm.Accounts alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope # Embed all files in layouts/* within this module. # The default root.html.heex file contains the HTML # skeleton of your application, namely HTML headers # and other static content. embed_templates "layouts/*" @doc """ Renders your app layout. This function is typically invoked from every template, and it renders the role-aware app chrome: header, nav, and flash group. `variant` picks which header chrome to render: * `:app` (default) — the full role-aware nav for every authenticated surface. Office roles (owner/admin) get the grouped office nav; everyone else gets the cleaner's minimal "My Day" link. Reads `current_scope` to tell them apart. * `:portal` — the client portal's minimal Home/Invoices nav. There's no user login in the portal, so this doesn't touch `current_scope` at all. * `:public` — a bare logo + "Client portal" link, for the landing page, the public booking funnel, and token-link pages that have no session to key a nav off of. ## Examples

Content

Content

<.link navigate={brand_href(@variant, @current_scope, @nav_role)} class="flex w-fit items-center gap-2 min-w-0" > Cleaner CRM
<.link :for={{label, path} <- @office_primary} navigate={path} class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm"> {label}
More <.icon name="hero-chevron-down-micro" class="size-3" />

Settings <.icon name="hero-chevron-down-micro" class="size-3" />

<.link navigate={~p"/field"} class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm">Field view
<.link :if={@variant == :app and @signed_in? and not @office?} navigate={~p"/field"} data-test="cleaner-nav" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" > My Day

<.link :if={@variant == :public} navigate={~p"/portal"} data-test="public-nav" class="btn btn-ghost btn-sm" > Client portal
<.theme_toggle />
<.icon name="hero-user-circle-mini" class="size-6" />
  • {@current_scope.user.email}

<.icon name="hero-bars-3" class="size-5" />
  • <.link navigate={path}>{label}
{render_slot(@inner_block)}

54	    end

68	    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
69	         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do

81	    else

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Users
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  # Make the remember me cookie valid for 14 days. This should match
  # the session validity setting in UserToken.
  @max_cookie_age_in_days 14
  @remember_me_cookie "_cleaner_crm_web_user_remember_me"
  @remember_me_options [
    sign: true,
    max_age: @max_cookie_age_in_days * 24 * 60 * 60,
    same_site: "Lax"
  ]

  # How old the session token should be before a new one is issued. When a request is made
  # with a session token older than this value, then a new session token will be created
  # and the session and remember-me cookies (if set) will be updated with the new token.
  # Lowering this value will result in more tokens being created by active users. Increasing
  # it will result in less time before a session token expires for a user to get issued a new
  # token. This can be set to a value greater than `@max_cookie_age_in_days` to disable
  # the reissuing of tokens completely.
  @session_reissue_age_in_days 7

  @doc """
  Logs the user in.

  Redirects to the session's `:user_return_to` path
  or falls back to the `signed_in_path/1`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, params \\ %{}) do
    user_return_to = get_session(conn, :user_return_to)

    conn
    |> create_or_extend_session(user, params)
    |> redirect(to: user_return_to || signed_in_path(conn))
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the user out.

  It clears all session data for safety. See renew_session.
  """
  def log_out_user(conn) do
    user_token = get_session(conn, :user_token)
    user_token && Users.delete_user_session_token(user_token)

    if live_socket_id = get_session(conn, :live_socket_id) do
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(live_socket_id, "disconnect", %{})
    end

    conn
    |> renew_session(nil)
    |> delete_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, @remember_me_options)
    |> redirect(to: ~p"/")
  end

  @doc """
  Authenticates the user by looking into the session and remember me token.

  Will reissue the session token if it is older than the configured age.
  """
  def fetch_current_scope_for_user(conn, _opts) do
    with {token, conn} <- ensure_user_token(conn),
         {user, token_inserted_at} <- Users.get_user_by_session_token(token) do
      conn
      |> assign(:current_scope, scope_with_active_account(user))
      |> maybe_reissue_user_session_token(user, token_inserted_at)
    else
      nil -> assign(conn, :current_scope, Scope.for_user(nil))
    end
  end

  defp ensure_user_token(conn) do
    if token = get_session(conn, :user_token) do
      {token, conn}
    else
      conn = fetch_cookies(conn, signed: [@remember_me_cookie])

      if token = conn.cookies[@remember_me_cookie] do
        {token, conn |> put_token_in_session(token) |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)}
      else
        nil
      end
    end
  end

  # Reissue the session token if it is older than the configured reissue age.
  defp maybe_reissue_user_session_token(conn, user, token_inserted_at) do
    token_age = DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(:second), token_inserted_at, :day)

    if token_age >= @session_reissue_age_in_days do
      create_or_extend_session(conn, user, %{})
    else
      conn
    end
  end

  # This function is the one responsible for creating session tokens
  # and storing them safely in the session and cookies. It may be called
  # either when logging in, during sudo mode, or to renew a session which
  # will soon expire.
  #
  # When the session is created, rather than extended, the renew_session
  # function will clear the session to avoid fixation attacks. See the
  # renew_session function to customize this behaviour.
  defp create_or_extend_session(conn, user, params) do
    token = Users.generate_user_session_token(user)
    remember_me = get_session(conn, :user_remember_me)

    conn
    |> renew_session(user)
    |> put_token_in_session(token)
    |> maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(token, params, remember_me)
  end

  # Do not renew session if the user is already logged in
  # to prevent CSRF errors or data being lost in tabs that are still open
  defp renew_session(conn, user) when conn.assigns.current_scope.user.id == user.id do
    conn
  end

  # This function renews the session ID and erases the whole
  # session to avoid fixation attacks. If there is any data
  # in the session you may want to preserve after log in/log out,
  # you must explicitly fetch the session data before clearing
  # and then immediately set it after clearing, for example:
  #
  #     defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
  #       delete_csrf_token()
  #       preferred_locale = get_session(conn, :preferred_locale)
  #
  #       conn
  #       |> configure_session(renew: true)
  #       |> clear_session()
  #       |> put_session(:preferred_locale, preferred_locale)
  #     end
  #
  defp renew_session(conn, _user) do
    delete_csrf_token()

    conn
    |> configure_session(renew: true)
    |> clear_session()
  end

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, %{"remember_me" => "true"}, _),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token, _params, true),
    do: write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token)

  defp maybe_write_remember_me_cookie(conn, _token, _params, _), do: conn

  defp write_remember_me_cookie(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_remember_me, true)
    |> put_resp_cookie(@remember_me_cookie, token, @remember_me_options)
  end

  defp put_token_in_session(conn, token) do
    conn
    |> put_session(:user_token, token)
    |> put_session(:live_socket_id, user_session_topic(token))
  end

  @doc """
  Disconnects existing sockets for the given tokens.
  """
  def disconnect_sessions(tokens) do
    Enum.each(tokens, fn %{token: token} ->
      CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.broadcast(user_session_topic(token), "disconnect", %{})
    end)
  end

  defp user_session_topic(token), do: "users_sessions:#{Base.url_encode64(token)}"

  @doc """
  Handles mounting and authenticating the current_scope in LiveViews.

  ## `on_mount` arguments

    * `:mount_current_scope` - Assigns current_scope
      to socket assigns based on user_token, or nil if
      there's no user_token or no matching user.

    * `:require_authenticated` - Authenticates the user from the session,
      and assigns the current_scope to socket assigns based
      on user_token.
      Redirects to login page if there's no logged user.

  ## Examples

  Use the `on_mount` lifecycle macro in LiveViews to mount or authenticate
  the `current_scope`:

      defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.PageLive do
        use CleanerCrmWeb, :live_view

        on_mount {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}
        ...
      end

  Or use the `live_session` of your router to invoke the on_mount callback:

      live_session :authenticated, on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
        live "/profile", ProfileLive, :index
      end
  """
  def on_mount(:mount_current_scope, _params, session, socket) do
    {:cont, mount_current_scope(socket, session)}
  end

  def on_mount(:require_authenticated, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if socket.assigns.current_scope && socket.assigns.current_scope.user do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:require_sudo_mode, _params, session, socket) do
    socket = mount_current_scope(socket, session)

    if Users.sudo_mode?(socket.assigns.current_scope.user, -10) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You must re-authenticate to access this page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp mount_current_scope(socket, session) do
    Phoenix.Component.assign_new(socket, :current_scope, fn ->
      {user, _} =
        if user_token = session["user_token"] do
          Users.get_user_by_session_token(user_token)
        end || {nil, nil}

      scope_with_active_account(user)
    end)
  end

  # There's no persisted "current account" selection yet (the account
  # picker doesn't write one anywhere), so every account-scoped page
  # would otherwise see a permanently nil `active_account_id`. Until
  # that selection is persisted, default a signed-in user onto one of
  # their accounts — the common case is a single-account owner, for
  # whom this is unambiguous.
  defp scope_with_active_account(nil), do: Scope.for_user(nil)

  defp scope_with_active_account(user) do
    scope = Scope.for_user(user)

    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.list_accounts(scope) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account: account, active_account_id: account.id}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  @doc "Returns the path to redirect to after log in."
  # the user was already logged in, redirect to settings
  def signed_in_path(%Plug.Conn{assigns: %{current_scope: %Scope{user: %Users.User{}}}}) do
    ~p"/users/settings"
  end

  def signed_in_path(_), do: ~p"/"

  @doc """
  Plug for routes that require the user to be authenticated.
  """
  def require_authenticated_user(conn, _opts) do
    if conn.assigns.current_scope && conn.assigns.current_scope.user do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You must log in to access this page.")
      |> maybe_store_return_to()
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/users/log-in")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(%{method: "GET"} = conn) do
    put_session(conn, :user_return_to, current_path(conn))
  end

  defp maybe_store_return_to(conn), do: conn
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount do
  @moduledoc """
  LiveView `on_mount` hook for surfaces that need an active company
  (account): a freshly-registered user has none, and every scoped
  context function guards on `active_account_id`, so letting them
  reach `/field` or the office pages crashes with a
  `FunctionClauseError`. Funnel them to account creation instead.

  Runs after `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth :require_authenticated` (which
  assigns `current_scope`) and before `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  on office routes.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    case socket.assigns.current_scope do
      %{active_account_id: nil} ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:info, "Create your company to get started.")
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/accounts/new")

        {:halt, socket}

      _scope ->
        {:cont, socket}
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole do
  @moduledoc """
  Restricts office-only surfaces — scheduling, timesheets (including
  the payroll CSV export), quality, invoices, clients, quotes,
  reminders, and the audit trail — to account owners and admins.

  A cleaner (or anyone with no office role on the active account) is
  redirected to `/field`, their own surface, with an error flash.

  ## Usage

  As a LiveView `on_mount` hook, listed after
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth`'s `:require_authenticated` in the same
  `live_session` (it relies on `current_scope.user` already being
  assigned):

      live_session :require_office_role,
        on_mount: [
          {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
          {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
        ] do
        live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
        ...
      end

  As a plug, listed after `:require_authenticated_user` in the
  pipeline, for controller routes such as the timesheet CSV export:

      pipeline :require_office_role do
        plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts

  @behaviour Plug

  @impl Plug
  def init(opts), do: opts

  @impl Plug
  def call(conn, _opts) do
    if office_role?(conn.assigns.current_scope) do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/field")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope

    if office_role?(scope) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/field")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp office_role?(%{active_account_id: nil}), do: false

  defp office_role?(scope),
    do: Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, scope.active_account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/app/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/app/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/app/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/app/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/app/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/app/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/app/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/app/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/app/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/app/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/app/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index
    end

    # Field surfaces need an active account: every scoped query guards
    # on `active_account_id`, so a freshly-registered user with no
    # company is funneled to /accounts/new instead of crashing.
    live_session :require_account,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default}
      ] do
      live "/app/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/app/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/app/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above. RequireAccount runs
    # first so an account-less user goes to company creation, not into
    # RequireOfficeRole's /field redirect (which would also crash).
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/app/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/app/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/app/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/app/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/app/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/app/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/app/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/app/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/app/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/app/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/app/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit

  # `:require_office_role` since a plug can't gate a live_session.

    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show

  # connect/callback URLs are registered with the external provider

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authenticated app surface

  # Every LiveView under /app/* is the "app" chrome (drawer + sidebar shell
  # via Layouts.app). The /app prefix is the source of truth that
  # distinguishes the app layout from the public/portal layouts (`/`,
  # `/book`, `/portal`, ...).
  scope "/app", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    # Authenticated, no account required. Account management lives here
    # (not gated by RequireAccount) so a user with no company yet can
    # still reach account creation instead of being locked out of the
    # one page that lets them create one.
    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index
    end

    # Field surfaces need an active account: every scoped query guards
    # on `active_account_id`, so a freshly-registered user with no
    # company is funneled to /app/accounts/new instead of crashing.
    live_session :require_account,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default}
      ] do
      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reviews, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/app/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above. RequireAccount runs
    # first so an account-less user goes to company creation, not into
    # RequireOfficeRole's /app/field redirect (which would also crash).
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount, :default},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/rate-card", QuoteLive.RateCard, :edit
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index

      live "/reviews", ReviewLive.Index, :index

      live "/settings/booking", SettingsLive.BookingPolicy, :edit
    end
  end

  # Office-only controller route (the payroll CSV export) — layered on
  # `:require_office_role` since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  scope "/app", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  # Authenticated routes that must stay at the root path (not under
  # /app): the password-update form posts here, and the OAuth
  # connect/callback URLs are registered with the external provider
  # (CodeMySpec's redirect URI), so they can't move.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password

    scope "/integrations/oauth" do
      get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
      get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
    end
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end

  # Reviews (story 853): the public token-link review page needs no
  # login — mirrors `/invitations/accept/:token`'s `:current_user`
  # live_session so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout.
  # No collision with the office inbox at `/app/reviews` — that lives
  # under the `/app` scope above.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :reviews_public,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/reviews/:token", ReviewLive.Public, :show
    end
  end

  # Portal (client magic-link) — no user auth. `/portal/access/:token`
  # exchanges a mailed/booking-issued token for a portal session
  # (plain `:browser`, like the reminder confirm/reschedule links
  # above, so `fetch_session`/`fetch_current_scope_for_user` still
  # run); every other portal route sits behind
  # `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth`'s own session check instead.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    get "/portal/access/:token", PortalController, :access

    live_session :portal,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.PortalAuth, :require_client}] do
      live "/portal", PortalLive.Home, :index
      live "/portal/visits/:id", PortalLive.Visit, :show
      live "/portal/invoices", PortalLive.Invoices, :index
    end
  end

  # Public booking funnel (stories 848/849) — no user auth, plain
  # `:browser` (like the reminder/reviews/portal public routes above)
  # so `current_scope` still mounts for the root layout. Both routes
  # share one view module, `BookingLive.Quote` — see its moduledoc for
  # why `BookingLive.Accept` isn't routed on its own.
  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :public_booking,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/book", BookingLive.Quote, :new
      live "/book/accept/:token", BookingLive.Quote, :accept
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireAccount do
  @moduledoc """
  LiveView `on_mount` hook for surfaces that need an active company
  (account): a freshly-registered user has none, and every scoped
  context function guards on `active_account_id`, so letting them
  reach `/app/field` or the office pages crashes with a
  `FunctionClauseError`. Funnel them to account creation instead.

  Runs after `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth :require_authenticated` (which
  assigns `current_scope`) and before `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  on office routes.
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    case socket.assigns.current_scope do
      %{active_account_id: nil} ->
        socket =
          socket
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:info, "Create your company to get started.")
          |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/app/accounts/new")

        {:halt, socket}

      _scope ->
        {:cont, socket}
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole do
  @moduledoc """
  Restricts office-only surfaces — scheduling, timesheets (including
  the payroll CSV export), quality, invoices, clients, quotes,
  reminders, and the audit trail — to account owners and admins.

  A cleaner (or anyone with no office role on the active account) is
  redirected to `/app/field`, their own surface, with an error flash.

  ## Usage

  As a LiveView `on_mount` hook, listed after
  `CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth`'s `:require_authenticated` in the same
  `live_session` (it relies on `current_scope.user` already being
  assigned):

      live_session :require_office_role,
        on_mount: [
          {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
          {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
        ] do
        live "/app/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
        ...
      end

  As a plug, listed after `:require_authenticated_user` in the
  pipeline, for controller routes such as the timesheet CSV export:

      pipeline :require_office_role do
        plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
      end
  """

  use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

  import Plug.Conn
  import Phoenix.Controller

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts

  @behaviour Plug

  @impl Plug
  def init(opts), do: opts

  @impl Plug
  def call(conn, _opts) do
    if office_role?(conn.assigns.current_scope) do
      conn
    else
      conn
      |> put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
      |> redirect(to: ~p"/app/field")
      |> halt()
    end
  end

  def on_mount(:default, _params, _session, socket) do
    scope = socket.assigns.current_scope

    if office_role?(scope) do
      {:cont, socket}
    else
      socket =
        socket
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.put_flash(:error, "You don't have access to that page.")
        |> Phoenix.LiveView.redirect(to: ~p"/app/field")

      {:halt, socket}
    end
  end

  defp office_role?(%{active_account_id: nil}), do: false

  defp office_role?(scope),
    do: Accounts.get_user_role(scope, scope.user.id, scope.active_account_id) in [:owner, :admin]
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.LayoutsTest do
  @moduledoc """
  Covers the role-aware app nav built for the UI/navigation pass: an
  office role (owner/admin) gets the full grouped nav, everyone else
  signed in gets just "My Day" — and the two must never both render.
  `/app/field` is reachable by both roles, so it's the one route these
  tests can share.
  """

  use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true

  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts

  describe "nav_role/1 and signed_in_home/1" do
    test "signed out has no role and no signed-in home" do
      assert Layouts.nav_role(nil) == nil
      assert Layouts.signed_in_home(nil) == nil
    end
  end

  describe "role-aware nav on /field" do
    setup %{conn: conn} do
      owner = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
      owner_scope = Scope.for_user(owner)
      {:ok, account} = Accounts.create_account(owner_scope, %{name: "Sparkle Co"})

      member = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
      {:ok, _member} = Accounts.add_user_to_account(owner_scope, member.id, account.id, :member)

      %{conn: conn, owner: owner, member: member}
    end

    test "an owner sees the office nav, not the cleaner's My Day link",
         %{conn: conn, owner: owner} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = conn |> log_in_user(owner) |> live(~p"/app/field")

      assert html =~ ~s(data-test="office-nav")
      assert html =~ ~p"/app/schedule"
      assert html =~ "Field view"
      refute html =~ ~s(data-test="cleaner-nav")
    end

    test "a cleaner sees only My Day, no office nav", %{conn: conn, member: member} do
      {:ok, _view, html} = conn |> log_in_user(member) |> live(~p"/app/field")

      assert html =~ ~s(data-test="cleaner-nav")
      refute html =~ ~s(data-test="office-nav")
      refute html =~ ~p"/app/schedule"
    end
  end
end

content.text:
I've completed the `/app` restructure and reported the results back to the team lead. Summary of what was done:

**Router** (`lib/cleaner_crm_web/router.ex`): Consolidated into one `scope "/app"` with three `live_session`s matching the spec exactly — unrestricted-but-authenticated (settings/accounts/integrations), account-required (field), and office-role-required (clients, properties, schedule, audit, quotes, quality, timesheets, invoices, reminders, reviews, booking settings). The timesheet CSV export controller route moved to `/app/timesheets/export` under its own office-gated scope. `POST /users/update-password` and `/integrations/oauth/*` stayed at root since the OAuth callback URI can't move. All public/token/webhook/portal/booking routes were left untouched, including `/reviews/:token`, which no longer collides with the office inbox now that it lives at `/app/reviews`.

**Layout** (`lib/cleaner_crm_web/components/layouts.ex`): Rewrote `Layouts.app/1` as three function-head clauses keyed on `variant`. The `:app` clause is now a drawer+sidebar shell mirroring `get_ai_traffic`, keeping our existing light/dark theme toggle. `:portal` and `:public` were preserved as the original top-bar chrome.

**Sweep**: Used a scoped Perl regex sweep across `lib/` and `test/` to re-prefix every route reference with `/app`, carefully excluding the paths that must stay at root (OAuth callback, reminder confirm/reschedule links, public review tokens). 166 files now reference `/app/`.

**Verification**: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean, `mix format --check-formatted` clean, 266 tests (including Wallaby journeys) passing, 143 spex passing — all zero failures.

This deploy needs a release rebuild since it touches the router and compiled release artifacts.
